findings.finding: The global forwarding market inflected violently inside Radiant's fiscal Q4 (Apr-Jun 2026) and after Radiant last spoke: Expeditors went from +16% EPS / +5% air tonnage / +4% revenue in the March quarter (reported 2026-05-05) to +51% EPS / +14% tonnage / +57% airfreight revenue / +32% total revenue in the June quarter (reported 2026-08-03), driven by the 28-Feb Middle East escalation removing ~12% of global air cargo capacity and pushing air spot rates ~+40% y/y in May.

The same June quarter crushed domestic truck-brokerage gross margin, which is the other half of Radiant's business: RXO's gross margin fell to 13.9% of revenue from 17.8%, and J.B. Hunt's brokerage purchased transportation rose 54% against 49% revenue growth, taking brokerage gross margin down 300bp to 12.5%, as truckload spot went to 42% of volume (+1,500bp y/y).

Three post-Q3 corporate actions line up as a pending acquisition: the 7 Aug 2026 amended-and-restated credit agreement extends the $200m revolver to 2031 at lower spreads and raises the acquisition accordion from $75m to $100m; on 31 Aug Radiant hired David Buss, previously CEO of DB Schenker's North America cluster, as SVP/COO explicitly to 'manage diligence and integration efforts for ongoing acquisition initiatives'; and the buyback went to zero in the March quarter (585,050 shares bought in Q1+Q2 FY26, none in Q3) while cash built from $22.9m to $39.7m.

CFO Todd Macomber sold down to 87,249 shares by 15 June 2026, roughly halving his direct holding across sales at $7.00 (late March), ~$8.50 (27-28 May), $9.30 (9 June) and $9.25 (12-15 June) — i.e. he was a persistent seller right into fiscal year-end and every sale was above today's $8.31.
